speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To help me understand the onset and nature of these symptoms, can you tell me when they first started and if anything makes them better or worse?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest, combined with specific triggers for your double vision (looking up or down), strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction disorder. To confirm this, I need to see the results of a Tensilon (Edrophonium) test, please REQUEST TEST: Tensilon_Test. Additionally, we should check for antibodies involved in this condition. REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR_Antibody.
